## Command Details

```text
Grant, use, settle, review, and list break-glass authorizations
(F057 T1-T4).
Break-glass is a distinct, one-use HUMAN authorization for a
production emergency — never a flag, a reusable token, or an
Agent-granted exception, and neither --yes nor --force ever routes
here. A grant is limited by one registered capability (an F052
runner capability pin runner:<runnerId>@<v>/<name>@<v> or an F056
external effect pin external:<effect-id>@<version>, verified
against its registry — break-glass reaches only what is already
governed, never arbitrary shell or HTTP), the exact target and
scope, environment, purpose, risk (low|medium|high|critical), a
credential class (none|scoped), a short half-open validity window
[validFrom, validUntil) of at most 24h at the injected governance
clock, an incident reference, and a mandatory post-review deadline
within 30 days of the window closing. Granting settles behind a
single-use committed human Decision (acceptance|approval with a
verified principal snapshot; Agents and service identities refuse
the slot — no self-grant) into the hash-chained append-only ledger
under .amber/breakglass/. `revoke` is a second single-use human
Decision that immediately blocks future use with a preserved
reason. Status derives read-time (granted|used|revoked|expired;
a terminal use wins, then revocation) and history is never
rewritten: revoked
and expired grants stay listable forever with their original
content intact. `use` spends the one-use authorization atomically
with the underlying admission under the ledger lock: the reference
must be the ALREADY-AUTHORIZED underlying request (an F056 proposal
id or an F052 runner requestHash) riding exactly the granted
capability at the granted target and scope (and environment for
runner requests) — a grant can never widen itself, a failed
admission never consumes, concurrent callers cannot double-spend,
revoked/not-yet-valid/expired grants refuse at the injected clock,
and the use event records the exact admitted request hash (a
re-chained use outside the window fails every read closed). A used
grant is terminal: it cannot be revoked or re-used, and status
used wins the read-time derivation. Every grant-facing name is a
closed slug and credential-looking material refuses: the audit
trail carries no secret. Nothing under this command executes
anything — the underlying capability still runs only through its
own governed F052/F056 surface.
An emergency attempt cannot disappear: `settle` binds the used
grant to the REAL underlying receipt (an F056 execution id or the
F052 runner request hash) and derives the outcome — including
failures and partial outcomes — and the declared rollback or
compensation linkage from the underlying registry, never from the
caller; a claim without a resolvable reference refuses, and one
settlement per grant records immutably. `review` is the mandatory
human post-review: outcome, necessity, impact, and follow-up
(non-empty, preserved) behind a single-use committed human
Decision, valid only after the grant ENDED (use, revocation, or
expiry) — one review per grant, and a late review is still
recordable but reads flagged. `status` projects the full lifecycle
at the injected clock: the grant with its use, settlement, and
review, plus read-time reviewOverdue (ended + past the declared
deadline + unreviewed) and reviewLate flags — Policy consumers can
fail closed on an overdue review, and review can never be silently
skipped. MCP surfaces only the approval-required grant contract and
never executes it, the ADR-0020 transport exception stays isolated,
and break-glass waives nothing.
```
